name: Chavez
label: Matador
lede: Two albums, one Beavis and Butt-Head cameo and riffs built like trap doors: Chavez never officially broke up, they just went off to play with Johnny Cash, write for HBO and direct movies, and left behind a pair of records guitar players still pass around.

eras.title: A spinoff of Wider, with a Harvard guy and a Hollywood kid
eras.text: Chavez grew out of the New York band Wider in 1993. The line-up was an unlikely one: a New Jersey guitarist who'd made records as a teenager, a Harvard graduate from a Boston hard rock band, and the son of the man who made Happy Days.

years.src: Wikipedia: Chavez · Matt Sweeney · Clay Tarver · Scott Marshall
years.h: Matt Sweeney and James Lo leave Wider and start Chavez
years.p: [[Matt Sweeney|256a32b5-7ba5-4560-bf1f-2632628a7e53]] and drummer James Lo, both from Wider, form Chavez in New York with guitarist [[Clay Tarver|7137b936-0210-478d-b9ff-f02c2aef8863]] and bassist [[Scott Marshall|ffcc505e-5b7d-4ac3-b333-11f6c8dcd401]].
years.xp:
Sweeney, raised in Maplewood and South Orange, New Jersey, had already made two records on Twin/Tone with his high-school band Skunk. Tarver, born in San Antonio and a 1988 Harvard graduate, had co-led the Boston band [[Bullet LaVolta|7913528c-6263-41c1-b488-aeae8fc291a9]], which recorded for Taang!, RCA and Matador before splitting in 1991.

Marshall is the son of director Garry Marshall and nephew of Penny Marshall.

years.h: Repeat the Ending, the single that started the buzz
years.p: Chavez's first single, Repeat the Ending, gets them a following in the New York underground fast.
Chavez records its debut over weekends in December 1994 and January 1995 with three producers: [[Bob Weston|7364260a-0a3e-4a6c-bcf8-b4e743c0b2c0]], Bryce Goggin and John Agnello.

eras.title: Two Matador records and a Beavis and Butt-Head moment
eras.text: In eighteen months Chavez released everything most fans know them for. The riffs were angular and asymmetrical, with dynamics that dropped out from under you, and critics reached for The Jesus Lizard, Blue Öyster Cult and Cheap Trick to describe them.

q: No debut of late combines guts and gray matter quite as fluently.
years.p: Matador releases Chavez's debut. Billboard says no recent debut combines guts and gray matter so fluently.
years.xp: The bassist is credited as Scott Anthony Masciarelli on Gone Glimmering, his family's original surname; his father Garry Marshall was born Masciarelli.

years.h: Beavis and Butt-Head watch Break Up Your Band
years.p: The video for Break Up Your Band, from Gone Glimmering, airs on MTV's Beavis and Butt-Head.
Chavez follows Gone Glimmering with the Pentagram Ring EP.

years.h: On tour with Guided by Voices and Bardo Pond
years.p: Chavez tours with [[Guided by Voices|6c85f4c3-026c-4c16-9a7c-f546f42ed0fb]] and [[Bardo Pond|2ad8bce1-8e55-48db-82ed-d98b52a3a13f]]. Matt Sweeney also fills in on bass for Guided by Voices' Under the Bushes Under the Stars tour.

q: A fine specimen of spare, brainy post-metal hard rock.
years.h: Ride the Fader, the second and last album
years.p: Matador releases Ride the Fader, co-produced with John Agnello and Bryce Goggin. Entertainment Weekly gives it an A.
years.xp: The album runs twelve songs, from Top Pocket Man to You Must Be Stopped, with Flight '96 and Our Boys Will Shine Tonight in between. Fans and critics tend to call it the band's best.

eras.title: Not broken up, just busy
eras.text: Chavez toured the US and Europe through 1997, then went quiet: few shows, no new music between 1999 and 2006. They never split. The members simply went off and did remarkable things elsewhere.

years.h: Chavez goes quiet without breaking up
years.p: From 1999 to 2006 Chavez releases nothing and plays only a handful of shows. According to Wikipedia, the band never officially broke up.

years.h: Matt Sweeney joins Billy Corgan in Zwan
years.p: Matt Sweeney forms [[Zwan|5af2629b-36de-486c-ad50-a89a28ff050f]] with [[Billy Corgan|3cbfd3e3-6d9b-4327-84ba-42cf646c98f9]] and [[Jimmy Chamberlin|48d3d17b-0bb8-44a0-9fb0-23f594bb4df3]] of the [[Smashing Pumpkins|ba0d6274-db14-4ef5-b28d-657ebde1a396]], with [[David Pajo|85188c46-d3ed-4517-ba78-5d06ec764f1c]] of [[Slint|2869c510-2679-4a3f-bf15-e5e8b49f2f28]] also in the line-up.

years.h: Clay Tarver co-writes Joy Ride with J.J. Abrams
years.p: Clay Tarver, who'd also made the Jimmy the Cabdriver interstitials for MTV, co-writes the thriller Joy Ride with J.J. Abrams.

years.h: Matt Sweeney makes Superwolf with Bonnie 'Prince' Billy
years.p: Sweeney and [[Will Oldham|eb51090c-662a-47a1-967c-c63292d9831a]] release Superwolf. He also plays guitar on Rick Rubin's Johnny Cash sessions, heard on American V (2006) and American VI (2010).

eras.title: Better days come back
eras.text: Matador gathered almost everything Chavez ever recorded onto one compilation in 2006, and the band started playing again, opening for Pavement and Sonic Youth and turning up at All Tomorrow's Parties. The members' day jobs got bigger too.

years.h: Better Days Will Haunt You, and Chavez plays again
years.p: Matador's Better Days Will Haunt You collects virtually all of Chavez's studio recordings, with new vocals on White Jeans. The band returns to select shows.

years.h: Scott Marshall directs Keeping Up with the Steins
years.p: AFI-trained bassist Scott Marshall directs the comedy Keeping Up with the Steins, followed by Blonde Ambition in 2007.

years.h: ATP I'll Be Your Mirror, Asbury Park
years.p: Chavez is picked for All Tomorrow's Parties' I'll Be Your Mirror festival in Asbury Park, New Jersey, organized with [[Portishead|8f6bd1e4-fbe1-4f50-aa9b-94c450ec0f11]]. In May 2012 they play the London edition at Alexandra Palace.

years.h: Matt Sweeney starts Guitar Moves for Noisey
years.p: Sweeney's web series Guitar Moves, where famous players show how they play, launches on Vice's Noisey channel.

years.h: Clay Tarver wins a WGA award for Silicon Valley
years.p: Tarver, later co-showrunner of HBO's Silicon Valley, wins the Writers Guild award for Episodic Comedy for the episode Sand Hill Shuffle. Sweeney tours with [[Iggy Pop|f37b3f31-b1f8-4b88-8cb5-b34f709b17d7]] that year.

years.h: Cockfighters EP, the first new Chavez music in decades
years.p: Chavez releases the Cockfighters EP, its first new record since Ride the Fader in 1996.

years.h: Matt Sweeney forms The Hard Quartet with Stephen Malkmus
years.p: Sweeney starts [[The Hard Quartet|bc67223b-b2b5-4431-92e6-620651978c6c]] with [[Stephen Malkmus|eaefd603-84c1-4db4-a72b-0cb718a0cc07]] of [[Pavement|36bfa85f-737b-41db-a8fc-b8825850ffc3]], Jim White and Emmett Kelly; they tour the world in 2025.
